articles: mayor wants city to improve parks letter to commission says grave and serious neglect has obtained in past mccarthy suggests expenditure of money and names the proposed bettermentstn a lengthy communication presented to the park commissioners at a special meeting yesterday mayor mccarthy drew attention to the various parks of this city tie said that public parks and squares that were neglected were detrimental to their respective districts while those well kept had a tremendous value as improvements for the whole city he said in no instance with which t have treated as mayor of san francisco is there more need for a just and equitable distribution of public funds than in the matter of the money expended in connection with the improvement of our public parks and squares we find ourselves in the possession of $357 000 plus 7 per cent on the increase of the valuation of the real and personal property over the basic figure of $492 000 000 used by the supervisors in arranging the budget which will bring approximately $15 000 making the grand total $372 000 to he devoted to parks and public squares under the management and control of the park commission grave neglect charged in looking over and carefully scrutinizing the public parks and squares outside of golden gate park i find that grave and serious neglect has obtained in the past and without desiring in the least to discuss situations over which i exercised no control or men with whom i had no association i desire to call to the attention of your honorable body that in the future a fair and proper distribution of the public funds allowed for the improvement of the public parks and squares of our city must maintain the following facts give a very accurate idea of what has heretofore been done in the premises taking market street from the hay to the ocean as the line of division wc find that out of a total of 36 parks and squares exclusive of golden gate park 20 of those parks or squares are north of market street 13 of which are improved 2 with some improvements and 5 without any improvements while on the south side of market street there are only a total of 16 public parks and squares and but 5 of these are improved 2 with some trifling improvements and 9 without any improvements at all the parks and squares which are improved north of market street present in every respect a beautiful finished appearance embracing as they do everything that goes to make a park really beautiful healthful and useful from a park standpoint on the south side embracing the great mission district the five parks so far improved do not present that appearance south park garfield square bernal park and the mission park are by no means as presentable from the standpoint of care and attention given them though they appear upon the public records as being improved as do washington square alamo square portsmouth square lafayette square duboce nark alta plaza jefferson square or marshall square all of which are on the north side of market street improvements suggested i would therefore respectfully recommend to your honorable board now that the parks and squares above mentioned with possibly one or tw o exceptions are taken care of except in the matter of maintenance that the parks located south of market street and embracing the great and thickly settled mission district be given your attention generally the mayor then called attention to what he considered necessary for various parks and the amount that would be required to carry out his suggestions for mission park $28 000 for balboa park $25 000 for holly park $11 000 for franklin square $25 000 for bernal park $2 000 for mckinley park $20 000 he also asked the commisioners to give due attention to the following sunnyside park at thirty third and stanyan streets fairmount park at bernis and fairmount streets lot between rhode island and de haro streets block between minnesota and tennessee streets block between channel and irwin streets block between delaware and massachusetts streets city and county hospital grounds at potrero avenue and twen ty sixth street lincoln park squares gate park the mayor said a suitable and up to date convenience station should be located within easy distance of the children s playground also one should be placed near the stadium a suitable building should be located within easy distance of the children s playgrounds with accommodations for the care and proper treatment of children by those who accompany them to the playgrounds in the park only one solitary room having for its purpose such accommodation is now to be found in the vicinity of the children s playgrounds this is by no means sufficient rather is it absolutely inadequate it can not and does not afford that degree of comfort and proper care to which the thousands of children who visit the children s playgrounds in the park are entitled drinking fountains should be placed at intervals throughout the park wherein an abundance of the same kind of water that is used by our citizenship generally throughout the city may be had by the thousands who visit the park as well as the workmen employed therein this at first sight may appear difficult yet it is quite easy to accomplish it can be either taken from a small center line of pipe with branches extended from take up the request of the san francisco motorcycle club for the privilege of the stadium race track for the american motor cycle club contest once a month in a third communication he said that in his university of california extension division announces its february programthe extension division of tin university of california recently announced its program for february the new schedule shows that thirty new courses will be started in san francisco during the month the work of the extension division through class instruction is constantly growing at the present time there are over nine thousand students enrolled in classes this year the extension division is offering new specialized subjects which are attracting many new students practically all of the courses starting in february will be given in the evening in the class rooms in the pacific building some of the courses which have proved the most popular in the past and which will start in february are salesmanship foreign trade commercial spanish and public speaking in the foreign trade class the demand for california products in foreign fields and the future of foreign trade on the pacific coast will be discussed aside from commercial spanish several language courses will be given in french and italian in the latter courses a number of singers and vocal students have enrolled stating that a knowledge of italian is invaluable in voice training persons interested in nature and out of door life are registering for six trips afield and the birds of california the former course consists of a series of saturday afternoon field trips to interesting localities in the bay region in the second course the students will be given laboratory study illustrated with specimens of the birds of california excellent laboratory and shop ecjuipment have been secured for courses in electricity chemistry and machine shop in these courses most of the instruction consists of actual experiments made by the students psychology of adolescence will be given by breitwieser of the university of california an authority on the subject this course is attracting parents teachers and social workers and others interested in the adolescent child a number of other courses are of particular interest to women they include dramatic reading play production and millinery jean campbell macmillan who directs various extension classes along dramatic lines will direct the play production course instruction in parliamentary law has proved so popular and met such a real need that the course is given a number of communities throughout the state other courses which will begin during the month are novel writing diatonic harmony history of the west mathematics and corrective gymnastics the extension division offices at 140 kearny street and 264 pacific building are now taking enrollments for the february classes

by daniel webster i have not allowed myself to look beyond the union to see what might lie hidden in the dark recess behind i have not coolly weighed the chances of preserving liberty when the bonds that unite us together shall be broken asunder i have not accustomed myself to hang over the precipice of disunion to see whether with my short sight i can fathom the depth of the abyss below nor could i regard him as a safe counselor in the affairs of this government whose thoughts should be mainly bent on considering not how the union may be best preserved but how tolerable might be the condition of the people when it shall be broken up and destroyed while the union lasts we have high exciting gratifying prospects spread out before us for us and our children beyond that i seek not to penetrate the veil god grant that in my day at least that curtain may not rise god grant that on my vision never may be opened what lies behind when my eyes shall be turned to behold for the last time the sun in heaven may i not see him shining on the broken and dishonored fragments of a once glorious union on states dissevered discordant belligerent on a land rent with civil feuds or drenched it may be in fraternal blood let their last feeble and lingering glance rather behold the gorgeous ensign of the republic now known and honored throughout the earth still full high advanced its arms and trophies streaming in their original lustre not a stripe erased or polluted nor a single star obscured bearing for its motto no such miserable interrogatory as what is all this worth nor those other words o delusion and folly liberty first and nion afterward but everywhere spread all over in characters of living light blazing on all its ample folds as they float over the sea and over the land and in every wind under the whole heavens that other sentiment dear to every true american heart liberty and ltnion now and forever one and inseparable

grocery price marking bill clears senatecalifornia afl cio legislation designed to protect the consumers right to know the price of commodities on the supermarket shelf have won senate approval on a 21 to 4 vote and was sent to the assembly sb 261 the bill sb 261 introduced by senator davie roberti d los angeles would require any grocery store or grocery department selling consumer commodities at retail to have a clearly readable price indicated on each item offered for sale need for the legislation was prompted by the recent implementation of the socalled universal product code upc a computerized pricing system already installed in some supermarkets throughout the state no law there is at present no state law requiring prices to be marked on individual items in grocery stores although this has long been the practice and serves as a major aid to consumers in comparing prices while shopping earlier this year t ie california labor federation called on afl cio unions throughout the state to write their state senators to urge them to vote yes on sb 261 vote yes the focus on this vital consumer measure now turns to the assembly and trade unionists and local inions and central bodies are urged to contact their assemblymen to urge a yes vote on sb 261 as it moves through the assembly

urges pinchot take air on reliefbryn mawr pa the women s trade union league conference held here recently made a demand upon governor pinchot that he undertake a series of state wide radio addresses attacking the gang politicians of the state for the treachery displayed in dealing with the relief crisis in his state the governor was asked by the conference to go to the people with the facts regarding the slashes in the appropriations to the various state departments in view of the fact that the newspapers have so beclouded the issues involved the conference felt that it was vital that a large number of people should be reached with the other side of the story speakers at the conference were john a phillips president of the pennsylvania federation of labor gertrude schermerhorn of the pennsylvania league for women voters john w edelman director of research for the american federation of full fashioned hosiery workers ewan clague research director for the community council and colston e warne of amherst university freda maurer president of the women s trade union league opened the meeting phillips told the conference that only well directed and consistent public agitation could now force any action for relief in the present session of the legislature economies so called would actually cost the state money and not save revenue miss schermerhorn showed other speakers stressed the fact that it was highly doubtful whether pennsylvania would be able to induce the federal authorities to fork out reconstruction finance corporation money for relief in this state in view of the refusal of the legislature to look out for its own citizens

recognition of heroic deedsin recognition of heroic deeds performed in 1927 bernard b randall of oakland and charles f ware of hanford are itij eluded among five employees of the pacific telephone and telegraph company awarded the vail medal for noteworthy public service other employees thus honored ate lucile g harer calexico nadler tacoma washington and ralph f murray san diego in addition to the medal awards the following employees were cited for honorable mention mrs mae mcgregor riverside gene vieve foreman mae barger and mrs ramona lynch berkeley joseph mohun san francisco joseph reed and emil brady san jose mrs may j walsh san rafael greenwell glendale i elizabeth rothaermel and mrs marie corbin newport beach robert borrow seattle and brown portland the citations of randall ware nadler and murray were each for the saving of a human life while lucile ilarer was cited for courageous conduct and devotion to duty in remaining at her switchboard through the severe earthquake of january 1 1927 j which partially wrecked equipment in the calexico central office an indication of the value of first aid methods taught telephone company employees is exemplified by the services of randall and ware while visiting on a telephone company cable barge randall was i attracted by an appeal for help from a man who had become exj hausted while swimming in san francisco bay removing only a part of his clothing randall dived and rescued the man and i promptly applied first aid methods ware while working on a telephone pole in hanford heard an i outcry from a power company employee who had fallen across high voltage wires on a nearby pole and promptly summoned a doctor and ambulance in the interim ware applied the prone pressure method of respiration and restored the man to consciousness

the oriental question discussed in the report of executive council of of lthe citizens of california are justified in viewing with alarm and apprehension the results of the japanese invasion in that state the japanese colonize together and have gradually driven out american citizens from the most fertile farm lands in the state they already have under cultivation 92 per cent of the celery 89 per cent of the asparagus 79 per cent of the onions 76 per cent of the tomatoes 66 per cent of the cantaloupes 79 per cent of seeds etc they undersell the american farmer because of their low standards of living not only have they acquired large areas of agricultural lands but they are gradually getting into the trades the gentlemen s agreement has proven to he a failure because the japanese in a cunning and stealthy manner have outwitted the intent of the law in 1918 11 143 new arrivals came to america in spite of the fact that the above agreement is supposed to exclude all except diplomats merchants and legitimate students in california alone there are over 100 000 japanese this peril is not only a serious condition for california hut it is a positive menace to our entire nation the american federation of labor is fully justified in taking a firm stand to do away with the gentlemen s agreement and in its place inaugurate a definite policy calling for total exclusion of japanese with all other orientals we should also go on record as favoring any legislation of the above character that may be presented in congress by the california delegation in the senate and house of representatives the chinese immigration laws absolutely prohibit japanese of any class from entering the country except by special permit this practically bars not only laborers hut students business men travelers etc from entering the country except for a very short period of time unquestionably the workers of different races colors or nationalities throughout the world have a common interest in their respective countries it is only by furthering that common interest that we can obtain the true objective of the labor movements the world over while the methods of industrial and commercial enterprise the supply of raw materials and of capital may have an equalizing tendency between nations the interchange of viewpoints and the establishing of friendly relationship between workers of the various nations are of far greater importance and tend more readily and effectively to cement the peoples of all nations in a peaceful concord today our people are confronted not alone with the possibility of greater competition with oriental labor and manufacture they are also facing the development of tendencies leading to the possible dangers of war no one recognizes more fully than do the american workers the burdens and sacrifices entailed in a contest between nations we have just emerged from a war out of which it is hoped that the opportunity for future wars would be lessened to the lowest possible degree if not foreclosed for all time to come we are confident that the japanese workers are equally desirous for continued peace as are the american wage earners we feel sure that the workers of japan would welcome whatever influence might be set at work to prevent a possible clash between the peoples of japan and our country limited suppressed and tyrannied the opportunity of these workers for protest is rendered almost voiceless and the american labor movement is looked to in the hope that existing industrial commercial and financial differences and difficulties may not be molded into tendencies leading to international conflict the executive council is of the belief that this entire subject should receive the most careful consideration and attention and that no effort be spared in protecting the interests of the workers here at home and in promoting good will and peaceful relations with the workers and nations abroad

constipationbeaumont s cornell fort wayne indiana this series of articles is prepared under the direction of the gorgas memorial institute which is organized to perpetuate the life work of the late major general gorgas in preventing unnecessary illness headquarters of the institute are at 1331 g street washington constipation is infrequent or insufficient elimination but no iron rule exists to show where diarrhoea ceases or constipation begins every person is a law unto himself the trouble may be due to actual organic changes piles fissures fistulas paralysis falling of the colon or it may be associated with an inflamed gall bladder or appendix often enough it is due to a diet too poor in roughage cellulose containing fruit or vegetables or too poor in vitamines which beneficially influence the bowel lining the continued strain of ambition and hard work may produce a lasting contraction of the colon thus impeding elimination a status which responds to relaxation and diversions most often constipation is due to careless neglect of going regularly to the lavatory colon worship is expressed in offerings of harmful purgatives prevalent ideas of auto intoxication are not true all the illfeelings which attend constipation result from pressure of fecal masses on neighboring organs and may be at once relieved by a simple saline enema a sensitive person may be rendered irritable by the lodgement of dried out feces in the colon but this organ has been overcharacterized as a villain and is constantly more sinned against than sinning colon consciousness just one of the modern abnormal states of mind is due largely to the clever advertisement of purgative manufacturers dread of constipation is in itself a common cause of the condition an attitude of confidence and faith is just as important here as in religion if such an attitude is adopted if a well balanced vitamin rich diet is eaten and if the individual will not be too absorbed in his affairs to devote a few quiet moments each morning to this simple ritual the matter will soon take care of itself if it does not a physician s care is required to search for organic hindrances

origin of first union of workersthe origin of the first union of workers in the world has long been in dispute and will perhaps never be satisfactorily settled many trades lay claim to the honor of having the oldest union in existence and one claim may be as good as the other the stone masons and stone cutters union for instance assert that tinstone masons and stone cutters engaged in the building of solomon s temple were organized into a trade union and we have no records to the contrary then comes the united brotherhood of carpenters and joiners of america and declares that the three sons of noah all carpenters organized during the erection of the ark and even called a strike on their old man and won out seriously however we do have authentic information that the first bona fide labor organizations or trade unions came into being along in the latter part of the bifteenth century among these were the carpet weavers of brussels the cutlery workers in england the clay workers in ireland and others ihe earliest known organization of painters was formed by a group of poor artists in zurich switzerland along in the sixteenth century and it is to these gentlemen we have been told that the brotherhood of painters owes the emblem of trade a pallette and brushes which is worn by organized painters the world overwomen need special training to resist the war frenzy dorothy canfield fisher prominent novelist and editor views daily misery and boredom as a powerful ally of war says social justice now will insure future peace specially contributed bydorothy canfield fisher a step forward toward understanding and hence toward mastering human problems is always taken when all human beings are recognized as being human forewarned is forearmed the traditional idea that a woman becomes a good mother through having given birth to a child is no more mistaken than that women can be counted on simply because they are born women and because many of them are mothers to withstand the collective hysteria that in times of war tears the covering of civilization from the majority of mankind and leaves their barbarism bared to view no women are human and without special training special discipline special experience cannot any more than unprepared and undisciplined men resist the frenzy that rises to about the same degree of trampling madness in a packed theatre where somebody has shouted fire and in a country where somebody has shouted the flag has been insulted yet one aspect in the life of modern women does from a veryunexpected source give them training experience and discipline that men rarely have does prepare them better to withstand at least one of the weapons with which war is defended and to understand more what measures are useful for preventing war we hear less nowadays than formerly about the desirability of an occasional war as necessary to preserve the virility of our manhood but a good deal is still said about the inevitability of war human nature being what it is two generations ago the same thing was said to mothers about the inevitability of quarreling and fighting among children women were told that the instinct to quarrel and fight was an inherent part of all vigorous healthful child life and they have found out not through theory but through actual experience with actual young human beings that there is no truth in that old conviction they have as mothers never did before made some study guided by sound psychologists of the principles that govern child welfare they have centered their efforts on providing those essentials the right food the right clothing fresh air sleep a har monious background and plenty of creative activity and they have seen that healthful children provided with these simple essentials waste no time in quarreling with each other because they are busy with occupations they like better women in charge of children have had it proved to them that quarrelsomeness is no sign of vitality and health but quite the contrary is an indication of something wrong as much as four degrees of fever indicates sickness they have learned this plain fact about human nature not from a lecturer or from a book but from observing human beings their instinct therefore when confronted with an angry and warlike frame of mind in anyone man woman or nation is not of resignation to the inevitable but of a quick inquiry as to what wrong factor in the life conditions is responsible for this sure sign of bad healthand here their experience with preventing quarrelsomeness among their children teaches them another sound principle of human behavior not so well learned by most men they have found that the evil causes for quarrelsomeness lie far back of the occasion when it shows itself they have learned that exhortations to behave themselves are of little use after the children have begun to fight they have been violently convinced by firsthand proofs that as little can be accomplished by arguing with the desire to fight once it is there as with a headache in both cases the only cure is to remove tjie causes which lie far far back of the symptoms intelligent men their attention fixed on economics by their habit of business feel that the real causes of war are economic intelligent mothers whose attention has been fixed on human nature by their care of their children feel that these well known and traditional economic causes the unscrupulous profiteers the wicked bankers the wire pulling of big business count more or less consciously on finding the bulk of humanity so restless an discontented with life that it will not be hard to stir it to war mothers know that healthy children provided with the essentials of life and this includes not only food and clothing but a fair opportunity for creative activity are hard to move to bickering their guess is therefore that misery and boredom in the daily life of humanity is a powerful ally of war that big business would have a harder time to create war sentiments if more people had their fair share of what they need such women will not be satisfied with attempts to resist the war fever only when it threatens they will feel that they are most surely working for peace in years to come when they work for social justice now when they give their full share of the effort to provide for all children the physical mental and spiritual privileges they know are needed to keep their own sons and daughters in health

of ancient egypt interesting relics coming to the united statesdespite handicaps caused by the war the pennsylvania university museum has acquired many relics unearthed at memphis by its egyptian expedition a vessel will be chartered to transport the relics the expedition started on its trip in march 1915 and continued explorations until last june when the shortage of labor and the high prices of materials due to the war caused a cessation in the work a representative of the roumanian government had obtained the concession of the whole site but the war intervened and the egyptian expedition offered the university party the choice of any portion an area near the colossi of rameses ii was selected because of the discoveries made in that region by an inspector of antiquities for lower egypt he had revealed what was apparently the room of a pharaoh s palace excavations by the party from the university museum proved the building to be the royal residence of menenptah who ruled from 1225 to 1215 the explorers found three layers of earth representing the ancient location of as many civilizations a large roman city had occupied the site of the topmost layer underneath which were large masses of masonry belonging to the period estimated to have been 332 30 and the lowest layer revealed ruins of the palace of menenptah at a total distance of from sixteen to eighteen feet below the surface level the palace which had been unharmed by the natives apparently had been a magnificent structure l imestone was the material used for the columns and framings while the otrter walls were of sun dried brick the eastern wing of the palace which was the first to be excavated contained magnificently decorated apartments where the pharaoh and his wife or wives spent their time the section of the palace that pleased the explorers most was the throne room six columns supported its roof the best preserved having a base of limestone with a horizontal band of inscription laid in pale greenish blue faience the lower part of the column had a row of sepals in relief springing from a broad band of gold between the tips of the sepals were large lotus flowers inlaid in faience panels showing a procession of nile gods bearing vases of water to the pharaoh and gilded relief figures of menenptah were promi nent features of a massive doorway that wtrs unearthed elaborate colored stucco pavements walls and small papyrus columns red yellow and blue being the colors of the principal patterns formed some of the striking interior relief features of the royal residence

the value of responsibility by barbara b huntingit seems a strange fact that one s neighbor s children are always wretchedly brought up we could suggest innumerable means and methods of improving upon the small fry across the way while even at the moment our own youngsters run shamelessly wild and are subject to much the same criticism from that neighbor herself but it is not in that spirit of criticism i make a suggestion rather in a hope that it may be of help to some mother who has a child or two with the attending problems to foster a feeling of responsibility in a child is one of the most important steps in starting him along the right road it will work wonders with him if he has his own little tasks duties about the house for which he alone is responsible the boy who keeps the grass trimmed along the walks after the lawn has been mowed who empties the ashes from the kitchen range each day sweeps the snow from the walks in winter picks up his clothes each morning and leaves his bedroom in order that boy is beginning well when he knows that his family depend upon him for the evening paper and the mail the responsibility thus imposed will strengthen the will to do it may be far easier for a mother to do a thing herself than to succeed in getting the boy to do it but in the end the effort will be found well worth the while and one which a thoughtful mother should feel it a duty to make the little girl who shares the task of dishwashing with her mother and whose duty it is to dust the living room before going to school in the morning that little girl is developing not only her abilities as a young housekeeper but those characteristics of unselfishness and service that are most essential in us all the question arises as to when we can begin to impose these little duties for surely a three year old cannot be expected to shovel snow no indeed but a child may be trained at a surprisingly early age to perform duties that lead as he grows older to larger things visit any kindergarten and children may be found doing things of which their own mothers never suspected them capable it is altogether too common a fault that mothers underestimate their children s capabilities many times mothers have come to our kindergarten and said why i had no idea johnny could do such a thing he never has at home for example children in kindergarten will put on their leggings coats overshoes and mittens without a murmur while at home they never even attempt to do this a two year old child may he taught to put away his toys take care of his coat and cap and run little errands about the house for his mother he cannot he trained too soon to wait upon himself don t make the common mistake of being a slave to your children teach them self reliance give them some responsibility you will be more than rewarded for your effort when they attain young manhood and womanhood

europe have been deeply interested the agitation which lias resulted in the enactment of the land bill at sacramento originated with the asiatic exclusion league this being true it is peculiarly appropriate that the league should pass judgment upon the law as finally enacted this the league has done by unanimous vote it concurred in the views of its president and declared the webb bill as amended to be unsatisfactory in other words the one organization most capable of expressing an opinion on this matter says that the great racket arising over the passage of the land bill is sound and it to signifying inothing that the law as enacted is so palpably a fraud that it deceives nobody had the state administration stood by its guns and not permitted a leasing clause to be tacked onto the webb bill as originally drawn the law would have been all that could have been desired so far as state legislation is concerned but with the law sanctioning leases which can be renewed for more than a low wages to women affect male workersin a pamphlet issued by the united states women s bureau it is stated that wages should be based on occupation and not on sex or race this is suggested from a well founded conviction the bureau states that low wages for women are a menace to the individual woman to the family and to the community as a whole the pamphlet is entitled short talks about working women several theories of low wage employers are demolished women are reminded that in the absence of wage commissions or labor organizations individual bargaining prevails compelled by the necessity it is stated a woman must work for whatever the employer will pay and the phrase individual gaining becomes a myth instead of a reality another myth is the claim that women merely work for pin money and are not a fixture in industry women s wages the bureau says are still based on the old theory that they have no family responsibilities as wage earners with results disastrous to that life and health for the maintenance of which they are responsible the lower wages for women in industrial occupations have a distinct influence on the wages of men any industrial group working for less than the standards which prevails in industry will have the effect of lowering the wage standard of all employees
